correctness.rationale: The determinant recurrence adds g_j² times the preceding minor, since (ig_j)²=−g_j². Parity divides (z+β)^m into Q_m and γQ_{m−1}, and the trace forces γ=mβ. The leading term of each backward remainder then recovers g_j² uniquely, with no sign ambiguity under g_j>0. With λ=1/2−m the monic Gegenbauer recurrence has no vanishing leading coefficient or denominator in the required range and gives the stated positive g_j² for all j<m. For degrees m and m−1 the eigenvalue in the differential equation is the same. The parity pieces of (z±β)^m solve that equation and match the monic solutions: both possible leading degrees are roots of the leading-term equation, but only one of those degrees lies in each parity, so no lower same-parity monic difference is possible. This gives exactly (z+β)^m. Nonzero nearest-neighbor entries force a nonzero eigenvector to have nonzero first coordinate and determine all other coordinates from it, so the sole eigenvalue has exactly one Jordan block. This checks the amplitude-loss convention and all m≥2 and β>0, not detuned sites, extra loss sites or robustness. Frozen verify_ep.py and VERIFICATION.md were inspected, not executed; their exact rational examples are consistency checks, not the universal proof.

evidence: At unit scale, write x=i/z. The Example 5.3 Weyl function is −1/z times O(x²)/E(x²), where E is the even binomial sum in x and mxO the odd binomial sum of (1+x)^m. The binomial coefficients give E(Z)=F(a,b;c;Z), O(Z)=F(a,b+1;c+1;Z) with (a,b,c)=((1−m)/2,−m/2,1/2) and ordinary F=₂F₁.

In DLMF 15.7.1–15.7.2 the ratio of regularized functions equals cE/O. Its t_k=k+1/2 and u_k=(k²−m²)/4 for both parities by substitution. Normalizing the nested fraction gives coefficients −u_k/(t_{k−1}t_k)=(m²−k²)/[(2k−1)(2k+1)] and u_m=0 terminates it.

With Z=−1/z² the resulting Weyl J-fraction is −1/(z−a₁²/(z−a₂²/(…))), so the no-loss real diagonal is zero and its positive off-diagonal squares are exactly those coefficients. Restoring β and k=m−j gives every frozen g_j².
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: This is an immediate continued-fraction evaluation of the prior exact inverse problem, not an assertion that the 2006 example literally prints the compact rational expression. The specialization already gives the full iff/uniqueness claim and exact formula.
searches: DLMF 15.7.1–15.7.2, Gauss continued fraction for a contiguous hypergeometric ratio

evidence: Let S=diag(1,−1,1,...) and R reverse the sites. J=RS(−iA/β)SR has first diagonal iγ/β, otherwise zero diagonal, positive off-diagonals a_k=g_{m−k}/β, and sole eigenvalue i when A has sole eigenvalue −β.
Example 5.3 constructs exactly this full-coalescence dissipative Jacobi matrix for all m, with loss scale m in its convention. Its general Weyl function and displayed cases match this transformation.

An irreducible Jacobi matrix is cyclic at its endpoint, so the prescribed repeated spectrum is already a single-block EP.

residual_risks: This assessment does not establish who first printed the compact formula or whether it also occurs in other exact tables. The already verified prior general theorem, example and direct fraction evaluation are sufficient regardless.

value.rationale: The explicit numbers are useful design data, and the Gegenbauer derivation can serve as an exposition. As a standalone finding, however, this is the identical known collapsed-spectrum construction with its Weyl fraction evaluated by a standard identity. The exact novelty proposed as a valuable narrow invariant is mechanically implied, and no additional physical or mathematical result survives that comparison. No substantive repair is supported.
